beliefs: f removes all whitespace characters (space, tab, newline, and Unicode whitespace) from the string [E1, E2, E3, E7, E9]
f lowercases all letters using Unicode-aware lowercasing [E1, E2, E3, E10]
f capitalizes the first character of the result only if the original string's first character is not whitespace [E2, E3, E8]
leading whitespace (space, tab, etc.) prevents capitalization of the first remaining character [E2, E3, E8]
empty string and all-whitespace strings map to empty string [E1, E2, E3]
digits and punctuation are left unchanged [E1, E2, E3]
the capitalize-first rule uses titlecase-uppercasing of the first char (e.g. ǆ becomes ǅ, ß becomes Ss, ﬀ becomes Ff) [E11, E13, E14, E15]
capitalization is applied to the first surviving character via titlecase-uppercase only (not full str.capitalize) [E12, E13, E14]
the rest of the string is lowercased before capitalization, so mixed-case non-ASCII like Ǆ becomes ǆ then ǅ [E12]
titlecase-uppercasing the first char uses str.title() semantics, which for ß yields 'Ss' and for ligatures like ﬀ/ﬁ yields 'Ff'/'Fi' [E11, E13, E14, E15]
an already-titlecase first char like ǅ stays unchanged [E12, E13, E14]
an already-uppercase first char like ẞ stays unchanged rather than being lowercased then re-titlecased, so the first char is titlecased only if it is not already uppercase/titlecase [E15]
notes: E15 shows ẞ (U+1E9E) stays ẞ, not Ss, so the first char is titlecased only when it is not already uppercase/titlecase; lowercase chars like ß/ﬀ/ǆ still get str.title() treatment. Updated predict to skip titlecasing when the first char is already uppercase or titlecase.
